title: How One-Pedal Driving Works (No Brake Needed?) 🦶⚡ #shorts

scenes.text: What if you could drive across town without touching the brake pedal?
In one-pedal mode, the accelerator does both jobs. Press to go. Ease off, and the car starts braking.
That's the motor running as a generator, turning your speed back into battery charge.
Nissan's e-Pedal slows you at up to zero point two g, like a real brake stop, so the brake lights come on.
Lift off fully and it adds the friction brakes, stops, and holds you, even on a steep hill.
But stay ready. On a full or cold battery, regen gets weaker, and hard stops still need the brake.
So is your brake pedal becoming a backup? Follow EV Drive.
